articles.title: Kyrie Irving Trade is 'No. 1' Question for NBA Execs Talking to Mavs Insider amid Latest Rumors
articles.summary: The Dallas Mavericks are off to an impressive 4-2 start, but it sounds like the sharks are already circling to try and pry away one of their best players.
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks are off to an impressive 4-2 start, but it sounds like the sharks are already circling to try and pry away one of their best players.

During Monday's episode of The Hoop Collective , ESPN's Tim MacMahon reported that Mavs star guard Kyrie Irving is one of the most talked-about names on the trade market this season.

A Kyrie Irving Trade to Elevate Eastern Conference Contender 🏀

"When I'm talking to executives and scouts around the league, when the Mavericks come up, it's the No. 1 thing people are asking me about," MacMahon said (11:38 mark).

At 34 years old, Irving is 15 years older than Mavs budding phenom Cooper Flagg. The duo combined for 68 points in a recent win over the Houston Rockets, with Irving leading the way with 35.

While Dallas is known to be rebuilding under first-year head coach Dusty May, the team's strong start has fueled hope for a potential playoff run this season.

MacMahon went on to explain that while Irving seemed like a top trade candidate entering this year, it will now take a lot to convince the Mavs to let him go.

"Going into this season, I would've said more likely than not he gets moved by the deadline, but I didn't feel super strongly about it," MacMahon said. "The more I see the team, the more I'm around the team, the more I think it's gonna be awfully hard to trade him. Not that there won't be a big market; there will be, but if they've got a chance to compete for a play-in, playoff spot, I just think it's gonna be really tough to move Kyrie."

articles.title: Redick Says Lakers 'Live on a Spaceship' as Luka Doncic Makes NBA History, 'Feels Like a Supernova'
articles.summary: After Sunday night's 131-125 win over the Toronto Raptors, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick couldn't help but revel in star guard Luka Doncic's latest history-making performance.
articles.body:
After Sunday night's 131-125 win over the Toronto Raptors, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick couldn't help but revel in star guard Luka Doncic's latest history-making performance.

"It feels like a supernova, but it also feels normal," Redick said after the win, per The Athletic's Dan Woike . "We live on a spaceship, and we're going at the speed of light at all times when he's on the court."

Doncic poured in 45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals and a block in the victory, which improved the Lakers' record to 5-2. His two-way impact made him the first player to record at least 45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists and five steals in a game.

While he's routinely faced criticism for his lapses on defense, Doncic seemed more engaged than ever against the Raptors. All 15 of his rebounds were on the defensive glass, and he also drew three charges, two of which were upheld after video reviews.

"Obviously, I'm not the best defender in the NBA, but I think this year I really took a step forward," Doncic said after the game. "Obviously, people are going to talk what they want to talk (about) me … But I know, and my team knows, that I think I'm better this year. And that helps the whole team, I think."

If Doncic remains committed to his defensive improvements, the Lakers will have a much better chance to contend for a title this year.

Los Angeles will try to keep the momentum going when it faces the Miami Heat (2-4) on Monday night.

articles.title: Men's college hoops opening-week primer: Florida-Miami, Arizona-UCLA highlight loaded slate
articles.summary: College basketball opens with a massive 183-game slate on Monday. Here are the biggest games of the week.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 college basketball season gets going across the country on Monday with 183 games in what is essentially a marathon slate of action. Notre Dame officially opened the season on Sunday with its comeback win over Villanova in Rome.

While there are only four ranked matchups this entire week, there are plenty of great games ahead on Monday and in the coming days. Top-ranked Florida opens against No. 14 Miami in Tampa, and then No. 5 Arizona will go up against No. 22 UCLA in Las Vegas to close the night.

Here's a look at the biggest games across the country over the first week of the new college basketball season

When: Monday, Nov. 2 | 6 p.m. ET Where: Benchmark International Arena | Tampa, Florida TV: ESPN

Florida is the top team in the country, and it's easy to see why. Thomas Haugh, instead of entering the NBA Draft where he would've been a lottery pick, is back for one more season alongside Alex Condon and reigning Defensive Player of the Year Rueben Chinyelu.

The Gators are the early favorite to win the national championship this season, which would be their second title in the past three seasons. Naturally, that gave them the No. 1 ranking in the preseason poll for the first time since 2006 .

Miami is a great first outing for the Gators, too. Jai Lucas led the Hurricanes to the NCAA tournament in his first season last spring, and Malik Reneau is back for a fifth season after averaging 18.9 points per game last season. Shelton Henderson is back, too, and Lucas picked up five-star recruit Caleb Gaskins. The Hurricanes are undoubtedly in a great spot, and should be able to hold their own in the ACC.

Getting past their in-state rivals to start the season, though, may be tough.

When: Monday, Nov. 2 | 10 p.m. ET Where: T-Mobile Arena | Las Vegas TV: TNT

The second major game on Monday night should be a great old Pac-12 fight.

Arizona, led by projected lottery pick Caleb Holt, is starting out the season with a top-five ranking after winning 36 games and reaching the Final Four last season. Motiejus Krivas was named the Big 12's preseason player of the year, and Ivan Kharchenkov is back after averaging 10.4 points per game last year, too. Oh, and Bryce James, LeBron James' son, is still at Arizona after redshirting last year. This is a team more than capable of running the table in the Big 12.

It will take a lot for UCLA to truly threaten the Wildcats, but it's not out of the question. Mick Cronin's group reached the NCAA tournament for a second straight year last spring, and they landed Jaylen Petty out of Texas Tech and star recruit Nikola Kusturica out of Serbia.

Arizona is the better team on paper, but Mick Cronin is very good at hanging with Arizona and Tommy Lloyd. Last year, Arizona only won by four points in a low-scoring affair in Inglewood. Expect a slow fight if UCLA is going to hang in there on Monday night.

When: Friday, Nov. 6 | 8 p.m. ET Where: TD Garden | Boston TV: TNT

We have to wait a few days for a title game rematch, but it'll be Michigan's first true test after last year's national title run. And things look very, very different for the Wolverines. Dusty May left for the Dallas Mavericks, first of all, which led to the program promoting Mike Boynton to replace him. They have also lost star freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. to an ACL injury that he suffered in Europe in September.

But Elliot Cadeau is back from last year's title team, and Kenny Noland transferred in from Columbia to help boost their lineup. Roddy Gayle Jr. was cleared for a fifth season of eligibility, too.

UConn is in a much better spot. The Huskies, who fell to Michigan in the title game in April, have Silas Demary and Braylon Mullins back. Dan Hurley, who just landed a two-year extension, got Nikolas Khamenia (Duke), Najai Hines (Seton Hall) and Nils Machowski (Wofford) in the transfer portal, too. Hurley has turned UConn into a basketball powerhouse once again, and his group looks more than capable of making what would be a fourth trip to the national title game in five seasons next April.

A revenge win over Michigan to start the season would be a huge first step.

When: Sunday, Nov. 8 | 1 p.m. ET Where: Capital One Arena | Washington, DC TV: ESPN

John Calipari regretted scheduling this game in the first place.

"Our schedule's ridiculous," he said at the SEC's media day last month . "Why I opened the season with Virginia, I must've been on crack."

To his point, the Razorbacks have Virginia, Indiana, Michigan State, North Carolina and Arizona all on their non-conference slate this season. It's going to be a very tough run before SEC play gets going, especially considering Calipari has led his team to the Elite Eight in his first two years with the program. That's a tough standard to live up to.

And Virginia, now in the second year of the Ryan Odom era, appears to have the program back on track after Tony Bennett's departure. The Cavaliers won 30 games last season and were able to hold their own in the ACC. He's got Chance Mallory back, and Thijs De Ridder is the preseason ACC Player of the Year.

This will be a fun game on Sunday afternoon, and one of just three ranked non-conference games the Cavaliers have on their schedule. A win here before ACC play gets going would be significant.

articles.title: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama still giving NBA Finals loss the silent treatment because of pain
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama apparently isn’t ready to revisit the San Antonio Spurs’ heartbreaking NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks. Nearly five months after fal...
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama apparently isn't ready to revisit the San Antonio Spurs ' heartbreaking NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks. Nearly five months after falling short of a championship , the superstar center reportedly remains reluctant to discuss the experience, even with the new NBA season underway.

French basketball reporter Maxine Aubin recently shared what he learned from conversations with Wembanyama's representatives. The Spurs star's reluctance suggests the disappointment of losing his first NBA Finals appearance still weighs heavily on him.

"I talked to his people, to his agents, and they said basically he does not want to talk about the finals," Aubin said in remarks shared by NBABase.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"From what I understand now, this is still something that hurts him, what happened in the finals. He does not really want to talk about it yet."

San Antonio lost the 2026 championship series to New York in five games despite Wembanyama averaging 26 points, 11.2 rebounds, and 3.6 blocks.

The defeat was particularly painful after the Spurs squandered double-digit leads in multiple games. Their most devastating collapse game came in Game 4, when the Knicks erased a 29-point deficit to secure a 107-106 victory.

Wembanyama previously acknowledged experiencing difficult nights following the series. During September's media day, he explained that dealing with those emotions was part of moving forward.

His reported reluctance to revisit the Finals doesn't necessarily mean he has stopped learning from the experience. He has continued working on his game while preparing San Antonio for another championship push.

For the Spurs, the challenge is turning that disappointment into progress without allowing last season's ending to define their next opportunity.

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg drops 37 points in win over Clippers, most for a Warriors rookie since Stephen Curry
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg looks like a future star in his brief debut with the Warriors.
articles.body:
We've come a long way since Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg called out Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić on opening night . Since then, the Warriors' rookie has generally backed up his trash talk, and has already turned in games with 26, 31 and 26 points.

But he saved his best performance — so far — for Sunday's contest against the Los Angeles Clippers. With Stephen Curry and Draymond Green sitting out, Lendeborg went off for a career-high 37 points in a 124-114 win over the Clippers.

That's the most points scored by a Warriors' rookie since … you guessed it … Curry back in the 2009-10 NBA season. During his rookie season, Curry exceeded 37 points just one time, when he dropped 42 points in the team's final game of the season. He did, however, cross the 30-point threshold eight total times.

After Sunday's win, Warriors coach Steve Kerr spoke extremely highly of Lendeborg, saying the team did not "expect" this, especially since Lendeborg is still learning the game, per ESPN.

"He's playing this way and he really doesn't know the NBA game yet," Kerr said. "The game is still really fast for him, but he's so skilled and so talented that he's making all kinds of plays. He's going to get a lot better."

Kerr later added that Lendeborg's emergence "changes everything" for the Warriors, who discovered the team is capable of winning games without their biggest names in the lineup. In addition to Curry and Green sitting out Sunday's game, the Warriors were also without Jimmy Butler, who is still making his way back from an ACL injury.

Lendeborg's performance should come as quite the surprise. Throughout his entire college career, Lendeborg scored 30 points just once. He's already exceeded that figure twice in seven NBA games. He's done it by hitting shots from beyond the arc, another thing Lendeborg didn't do much until his final year in college.

That long-range prowess was on display Sunday, as Lendeborg went 13 of 19 from the field, including six of 11 from 3-point range. It marked the second time in his NBA career Lendeborg has made six 3-pointers in a game.

While his output was impressive, it may not continue when Curry and Green return Monday. Lendeborg said he forced himself to step up his game with Curry out, per ESPN.

"Whenever Steph's not in the game, it's my opportunity to try to be the leader, be the main guy on the team," Lendeborg said.

But if the rookie can continue to put up big performances, it won't be long before he's a more regular staple of the team's offense, even in games where Curry is active.

articles.title: NBA Stock Up, Stock Down Nov. 2: Grizzlies, Trail Blazers, Mavericks rocket up rankings
articles.summary: Meanwhile, teams battered with injuries (and there are a lot of them) are falling down the rankings.
articles.body:
Welcome to our weekly look at the teams that are the most dramatic risers and fallers in the NBC Sports NBA Power Rankings. Undefeated Memphis is flying up the rankings, while a lot of injured teams are falling back.

The last undefeated team in the NBA shot up 12 spots in the NBA power rankings this week to No. 5, and this is a team I had ranked 25th before the season started. The soft schedule to start the season helps, but the chemistry of the front line between Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey has been phenomenal, and Ty Jerome could not have had a better start to the season.

Maybe the best story at the start of the season is the entertaining Portland Trail Blazers, who jumped up seven spots in this week's rankings to No. 9. The good news is how well Ja Morant, Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija are playing off each other. The bad news is Morant is out with a hamstring strain and will miss a month or more.

Nobody flew up the rankings faster this week than the Warriors, who jumped 16 spots to No. 12. Golden State looked shorthanded and dead in the water while losing its first three games, then Stephen Curry started playing like he was 28 and not 38, and Yaxel Landeborg emerged as a star. Golden State has rattled off four straight wins, and the last of those came without Curry (but 37 from Landeborg).

The NBA's giant killers, knocking off two undefeated teams — Oklahoma City and Houston — in the same week, which vaulted them up 11 spots in the rankings to No. 10. They are doing it behind Cooper Flagg, who is making a leap in his second season (26.8 points, 6.6 assists and six rebounds a game) and looks like an All-NBA player in just his second season.

Other risers of note: Houston moved up just two spots to No. 1 in the rankings; Boston just keeps on winning behind a hot Jayson Tatum and moved up five spots to No. 4.

No team has been hit harder by devastating injuries this young season than the Thunder, who have lost three starters: Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are out for most (or, more likely, all) of the season, while Chet Holmgren is going to miss a couple of months with treatment on his knee. OKC will still win games with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Ajay Mitchell leading the offense, but it is not the same team, and it fell 10 spots and out of the top 10 entirely.

With Anthony Edwards out to have knee surgery, the Timberwolves fell nine spots back to No. 13 in the power rankings. The offensive shot-creation load now falls on LaMelo Ball, and history suggests that will be a roller coaster of highs and lows, but he's got to build better chemistry with Rudy Gobert if this is going to work. Edwards got the surgery now so he can be back around Christmas/New Year's and be good when it matters most for the team.

The Raptors had to know they were going to spend time without Kawhi Leonard this season and that has come due to knee swelling. What was shocking was how the Raptors' defense fell apart without him, and the team is 1-3 since he went out, so they fell seven spots in the power rankings to No. 14.

articles.title: Lakers Must Trade for Trey Murphy III, Herb Jones to Help Luka, LA's Title Chances Amid NBA Rumors
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are one of a handful of teams interested in potentially acquiring Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones from the New Orleans Pelicans, per Clutch Points' Chris Dodson.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are one of a handful of teams interested in potentially acquiring Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones from the New Orleans Pelicans, per Clutch Points' Chris Dodson .

"Multiple teams are monitoring the situation surrounding both Jones and Trey Murphy III. Among those mentioned by sources or seen in an arena are the Houston Rockets, Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls, Washington Wizards, Golden State Warriors, Oklahoma City Thunder, San Antonio Spurs, Detroit Pistons, and Memphis Grizzlies."

The Lakers are 5-2 thus far in the 2026-27 NBA season, and while there has been plenty to be excited about on the court, there are two areas that the team must improve to contend in the loaded Western Conference: defense and on the wings.

Murphy has great length and, more importantly, is mobile on the wing. Jones shares similar length but has even better anticipation than his teammate, allowing him to jump routes and shots.

It is unlikely the Lakers could make a trade for both players, if for no other reason that they simply do not have the assets necessary to pull it off. Such a deal would drain the team's draft picks, with only the 2031 and 2033 picks unprotected.

Even adding one of the two would be a significant upgrade for a team that has NBA title aspirations, with one of the league's best players, Luka Doncic, leading the way. It will not be easy, and would likely still cost the organization significantly but the team has to at least take its shot.

Through the first seven games, Doncic is averaging 37.7 points per game, is shooting 43.2 percent from beyond the arc, 48.2 percent from the floor, and is tallying 8.2 rebounds and 7.3 assists.

To maximize the team's potential and make the most of Doncic's otherworldly play, the team has to improve those two areas if it wants to make a legitimate run at the Larry O'Brien Trophy. Making a deal for Murphy or Jones is the best, most surefire option.

articles.title: Michael Wilbon Announces Indefinite ESPN Leave of Absence Amid 'Multiple Health Issues'
articles.summary: ESPN personality and Pardon the Interruption co-host Michael Wilbon announced Monday that he is taking an indefinite leave of absence due to "multiple health issues" in recent months.
articles.body:
ESPN personality and Pardon the Interruption co-host Michael Wilbon announced Monday that he is taking an indefinite leave of absence due to "multiple health issues" in recent months.

Pardon the Interruption recently celebrated its 25th year on the air, with Wilbon and Tony Kornheiser as its hosts for the duration of its run.

" PTI continues with the same level of success that it had 25 years ago," the show's longtime executive producer, Erik Rydholm, told ESPN . "And the reason for that, for us, is Tony and Mike. Because people feel connected to them and their relationship. It feels familiar to them, with family being the essence of familiar. They feel connected to it, and that carries them through. ... They have a dynamic where one plus one equals something more than two."

Last year both Wilbon and Kornheiser reportedly signed extensions with ESPN to continue broadcasting PTI through 2028.

Alongside hosting PTI , Wilbon has also been a part of ESPN and ABC's NBA coverage.

His bouts with medical issues in the past included a heart attack in 2008, a diagnosis of Type II diabetes and diabetic ulcers in both of his feet.

As for his potential replacement, Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing noted that "When Wilbon or Kornheiser are absent, PTI goes to a regular bench of fill-ins including Frank Isola, Pablo Torre, and Mina Kimes."

But replicating the Wilbon-Kornheiser dynamic is impossible.

"They are not the same person," Rydholm noted. "One of the reasons the dynamic works is that Tony is more of an instigator, an agitator, and Mike is more of a counter-puncher, and so Tony will lay down what he sees, and often what he sees is sometimes in response to what he presumes Mike is going to say, what Mike thinks. And so Mike is just then all fired up, and he'll start swinging back in boxing parlance, and everything escalates. And it escalates with what I think is really rare about the partnership in that you know there's a foundation of love and friendship. ... I've never met, and I've never seen in my life, a couple in a relationship who can fight like cats and dogs and neither of them takes it personally. [Kornheiser and Wilbon] actually enjoy it, and everything's OK. My impulse is to try and fix everything. They love it. They find joy in those interactions."

Long-time ESPN personality Michael Wilbon announced Monday that he's stepping away from the network for an uncertain amount of time due to "multiple health issues." The 67-year-old announced the news in a statement, saying he's hoping to be back on television before long.

Wilbon did not provide specifics into his health struggles, merely saying it was not due to alcohol usage or sports gambling.

"This isn't retirement, but it is a trip to the injured list. Hopefully not an extended one. Struggles with multiple health issues in recent months lead me to take an indefinite leave of absence from my PTI and NBA duties at ESPN and ABC. "Probably, I should have listened to medical professionals and people closest to me, yep Kornheiser included, who saw worrisome signs in recent years that suggested I take time away earlier. But I didn't. "And as one close friend has said as my issues have become bigger, "the bill has come due." The struggles are all health related, not to alcohol (I'm not swearing off the now-and-then Kier Royale) and not to gambling (those winds of change I find loathsome). "I have loved sparring and hosting PTI with Tony every single day these past 25 years. And I'm incredibly grateful for the support and encouragement of my colleagues as I take this time away to concentrate on me, specifically on my well-being. I have no idea exactly how this part of my journey will wind up. The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony."

articles.summary: Longtime sportswriter and television commentator Michael Wilbon is taking an extended break from “Pardon the Interruption,” the long-running ESPN debate show, to focus on his health. articles.body:
Longtime sportswriter and television commentator Michael Wilbon is taking an extended break from “Pardon the Interruption,” the long-running ESPN debate show , to focus on his health.

Wilbon, in a statement posted Monday to social platform X, said he was stepping back from the show indefinitely, though he did not give specifics on what was ailing him.

“This isn’t retirement but it’s a trip to the injured list,” he wrote, saying he “should have listened” to people urging him to step back from the program to focus on his health sooner.

“The struggles are all health related,” the commentator continued, clarifying his current condition has nothing to do with alcohol or gambling, which he joked he still enjoys “now and then.”

“I have no idea exactly how this part of my journey will end up,” Wilbon added. “The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony.”

He has hosted the show with fellow sportswriter Tony Kornheiser since 2001, presiding over one of ESPN’s most popular evening news and debate programs.

A former sports columnist at The Washington Post, Wilbon has also been a staple of ESPN’s NBA coverage in recent seasons and is a member of the DC Sports Hall of Fame.

He has been outspoken on politics on several occasions, voicing support for athlete social justice protests in 2020 and more recently defending President Trump’s attendance at an NBA Finals game in New York City .

articles.title: Angel Reese Reveals Break from Podcast After WNBA Season, 'I'm Dedicating This Offseason to Myself'
articles.summary: After a long WNBA season that ended with the Atlanta Dream losing in the Finals, Angel Reese plans to spend her offseason recovering and getting better.
articles.body:
After a long WNBA season that ended with the Atlanta Dream losing in the Finals, Angel Reese plans to spend her offseason recovering and getting better.

That means she'll be taking time off from her podcasts as she is "dedicating this offseason to myself," she announced on Monday on Instagram

Dream Unrivaled Trios We'd Like to See 🤩

Reese is coming off the best season of her young career, averaging 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game. She earned her first Defensive Player of the Year award as well as an All-WNBA Second Team nod and an All-Defensive First Team honor.

Behind Reese's outstanding season, the Dream, who traded for Reese last offseason, finished the regular season 30-14. They swept the Washington Mystics and the New York Liberty en route to their first WNBA Finals since 2013, but came up short against the Golden State Valkyries in seven games.

"It's tough. Especially with a good group, a great group, that I've honestly had the honor to battle with all year," she told reporters after losing Game 7 on Saturday. "They changed my life, and I'm so grateful for them. And I'm so thankful for them. It is tough in the moment, but we'll be back. And I always say, 'Delayed not denied.' This is only year three—[my teammates have] a lot more years left too—but I'm just really grateful I got to go to war with this group. I would do it again, all over again."

Unfortunately for basketball fans, Reese's break this offseason seemingly means she won't participate in Unrivaled, which she has played in the last two seasons. She was not included among the 48 players announced for this year's roster.

But the Dream star will surely be fired up heading into the WNBA season as she tries to get her squad back to the Finals.

articles.title: Spike Lee hopes the Knicks won't visit the White House, warns owner 'can’t force them'
articles.summary: Spike Lee says he hopes the New York Knicks refuse to visit the White House, claiming owner James Dolan cannot force players to meet President Donald Trump.
articles.body: Director Spike Lee told Variety he hopes the New York Knicks will refuse to meet with President Donald Trump, as other teams have done after winning championships. The Knicks won the 2026 NBA Finals by defeating the San Antonio Spurs 4-1 in the championship series in June, ending a 53-year title drought for the franchise. Lee, a devoted Knicks fan and critic of Trump, was asked by Variety's Marlow Stern about reports that some players did not want to visit the White House and would rather skip the longstanding tradition. "Apparently, the team owner, James Dolan, who we know is a Trump pal, is trying to force them to visit the White House, but the team doesn’t want to," Stern told Lee. KNICKS OWNER CONFIRMS CHAMPIONSHIP CELEBRATION INVITE TO WHITE HOUSE WHILE SEAHAWKS VISIT ON BACK BURNER "He can’t force them!" Lee replied. "It’s been years since the last NBA team has gone. They’re not going. I hope they don’t go! I hope they don’t go." "Trump also messed up Game 3 of the Finals for the Knicks," Stern argued. "They’d won 13 playoff games in a row until Dolan invited Trump to the game and ruined their mojo." "That was not just an accident!" Lee responded. They were referring to how Trump, a native New Yorker and longtime Knicks fan, was invited to attend the game at Madison Square Garden by Dolan. The Spurs won the game that day, and many New Yorkers, including "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin, blamed the Knicks’ loss on Trump’s attendance. But I think there's a much bigger lesson here, especially for young Americans, and it's one Stephen A. Smith articulated very well after facing criticism for having dinner with President Trump." "You don't have to agree with the president, you don't even have to like him," she continued. "But he is the President of the United States. And if you genuinely care about bringing Americans together, finding solutions, or improving the lives of people in your community, you have to be willing to sit down with people you disagree with." "This is a lesson that’s incredibly important for young men to learn," Pipko added. "These are individuals who have large followings and should be focusing on inspiring the next generation and teaching them about what matters. Spike Lee's position puts political opposition ahead of an opportunity for dialogue, change, or opportunity. articles.title: New Kyrie Irving Trade Rumors Reveal Mavs' Stance on PG amid Heat Buzz, Calls From NBA Teams
articles.summary: It doesn't sound like the Dallas Mavericks have any interest in trading Kyrie Irving.
articles.body:
It doesn't sound like the Dallas Mavericks have any interest in trading Kyrie Irving.

"June is when the Mavs started telling teams Kyrie Irving is not available," NBA insider Marc Stein reported Monday. "You can call for him, we are not making him available."

His comments come after ESPN's Shams Charania appeared on the Pat McAfee Show late last month and reported "a slew of teams" were monitoring Irving (eight-minute mark). He also specifically highlighted the Miami Heat as a team that could be interested.

"I'm sure knowing the Heat, they're going to be monitoring Kyrie Irving," Charania reported (11:00 mark). "But there's gonna be several teams interested in Kyrie Irving. The question is if you're Miami, what can you give for Kyrie Irving? You already traded away three first-round picks and a swap and other assets to go get Giannis Antetokounmpo to bring to this team."

What's more, ESPN's Tim MacMahon reported Monday on The Hoop Collective that Irving is "the No. 1 thing people are asking me about" when he discusses Dallas with other executives and scouts in the NBA (11:38 mark).

Notably, Stein said much of the Irving buzz has come from the outside and not the Mavericks themselves.

"The media speculation and chatter about a Kyrie trade has increased, and I'm like, 'guys, the Mavs are 4-2. If they were 1-5 or even 2-4, I guess maybe then you could understand,'" he said. "But things have gone so well early, and the Mavs have consistently told teams they don't even want to field your call on Kyrie Irving."

It has been an impressive start for the Mavericks, and Irving is a major part of that while averaging 21.4 points per game.

However, he also turns 35 years old this season and has a player option for the 2027-28 campaign. Dallas is building around 19-year-old Cooper Flagg, so it is fair to speculate about Irving's immediate future since he is not on the same timeline as the franchise cornerstone.

He also isn't guaranteed to be in Dallas next season because of the player option, so the Mavericks may look to get something back for him if they do start to struggle as the season progresses.

For now, though, they reportedly aren't interested in trading him.
